text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- The cabinet decided to lower the monthly crawling peg devaluation of the forint from 1.2 to 1.1 percent starting in April and to reduce the customs surcharge from 4 to 3 percent from May 15. The surcharge was reduced to 4 percent today. The cabinet plans to submit the pension proposals to Parliament on April 18.
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn said Sunday that Hungary and Romania should be admitted to NATO simultaneously.
- Farmers across Hungary in 220 locations will block one lane of two-lane roads today.

- Hungarian agriculture is expected to take in $6 billion to $7 billion in export revenues in each of the next few years, according to a draft national agrarian programme outlined by Agriculture Minister Frigyes Nagy.
-The European Christian Democratic Union is organising a meeting between factions within the Christian Democrats in a bid to restore party unity, EUCD president Wim van Velzen said.
- SBC Warburg, one of Europe's leading investment banks, has undertaken to find a strategic investor to purchase 15-20 percent of Postabank, said bank CEO Gabor Princz.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The Smallholders' party leads a recent popularity poll with 29 percent, followed by the Young Democrats with 24 percent and the Socialist with 22 percent.
- Democratic Forum President Sandor Lezsak has written an open letter to Hungarian society, saying that Hungary has broken in two and its internal security has been shaken.
- Welfare Minister Mihaly Kokeny and his regional counterparts are attending a two-day conference in Washington, starting today, on health sector financing.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- The first stage of the oral arguments in the International Court of Justice trial of the Gabcikovo hydropower project between Hungary and Slovakia ended on Friday. (Sat.)

- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs came home from an official visit to Washington on Friday saying the US is firmly determined to carry out a scheduled expansion of NATO and that Hungary continues to have a good chance of joining the military alliance.

- Young Democrats president Viktor Orban expressed his party's full support for farmers' grievances, including the most radical demands for the immediate withdrawal of the social insurance and tax regulations.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The country's foreign trade deficit was $344 million in January, according to preliminary data.
- The average gross monthly wage of a full-time private sector worker was HUF 52,350 in January.
- Investors can subscribe shares of the curtain manufacturer Garadenia from today at a price of HUF 1,465.
- The property of the bankrupt refrigeration company Goldsun will be actioned off, the liquidator has announced.
NAPI GAZDASAG

- The list of companies earmarked for the third round of the simplified privatisation programme will be published late this month, said executive director Imre Ragats of the State Privatisation and Holding Co.
- The privatisation of Budapest's 182 pharmacies has been completed, said Mayor Gabor Demszky.
